This administration makes me sick and they have no clue. Check the math, cause the numbers do more damage than any insult could.

The Houthis declared the blockade on July 20. Bab al-Mandeb carries about 12 percent of global trade and a quarter of the world’s container traffic. Saudi crude loadings through that strait already dropped 36 percent in two weeks, from 9.5 million barrels a day down to 6.1 million.

And here’s the part that matters. Since Hormuz went effectively shut back in February, Saudi Arabia had rerouted more than 70 percent of its exports to Yanbu on the Red Sea coast. So the workaround for the first chokepoint runs straight through the second one. Close them both and a quarter of the world’s oil and gas supply is at risk.

That right there tells you nobody in that room asked what the other side does next. That’s checkers. You take a piece and feel good about it. Chess is knowing what he does three moves after you take it.

Now watch it get worse.

A Shahed drone costs somewhere between twenty and fifty thousand dollars to build. Shooting one down with a Patriot PAC-3 costs about four to five million. Every single time. They are not trying to beat our defenses. They are trying to make us spend our way out of ammunition, and it is working.

As of December, the Missile Defense Agency had 414 SM-3s and 534 THAAD interceptors. That is the whole inventory. A Pentagon official told the Washington Post we do not have enough THAAD to safely sustain the air campaign, and that the White House may not understand how bad the depletion is. Lockheed delivered 620 Patriot interceptors in all of 2025. That is 1.7 missiles a day for every ally we supply. Each one takes 24 months to build and 30 months for the rocket motor. The ones ordered in April do not show up until 2028 at the earliest.

So we spend around a trillion dollars a year, more than the next several countries combined, and we are rationing the one thing this war actually consumes.

And the same systems burning up in Iran, the THAAD and the Patriot and the SM-3 and the Tomahawk, are the exact ones we would need if China moved on Taiwan. CSIS said it plain. Keep this up and you open a window of vulnerability in the Pacific. So the move they made in the Middle East just weakened the board in the place that matters most. Three moves out, and they never saw it.

None of this is just and none of it is virtuous. A war does not get graded on how well it was run.
